title: iMOD Coupler product integration
findings: Upstream DriverType currently contains metamod, ribamod and ribametamod only.
Upstream get_driver is a hard-coded product registry and exposes no external entry-point/plugin mechanism.
The actual MetaMod driver owns the coupled timestep lifecycle; F-GC50 must integrate at this product layer rather than duplicate it inside SWAP5.
F-GC49D Python runtime consumes a positive pre-existing opaque Fortran context handle.
The F-GC49D fixture can create a test context but remains qualification-only and is ineligible for product bootstrap.

PPA-WU01 is canonically admitted and supplies the previously missing production-side Fortran/FMR owner for persistent state, participant registry, mass ledgers and per-window F-GC49D context materialization.
F-GC49D correctly remains an opaque-handle consumer at the C/Python seam; resolving B2 does not introduce Python ownership or a create-context C ABI.

Mapping a future iMOD Coupler product configuration into the restricted admitted PPA-WU01 typed profile remains implementation work inside F-GC50 once a real upstream driver-registration route is available.

blockers.description: Actual iMOD Coupler product registration requires an upstream source change, but the connected repository permission is read/pull only.

exclusions: Python ownership of SWAP/FMR state or ledgers
